costaxis_branch_line: on the two grid points both non-empty axes price, the two order the points identically, so the ORDERING is stable across them while the COST is not; a stable ordering is not evidence that either axis resolved the cost

costaxis_demo_line: one demonstration operating point, theta 0.525 at 0.5240 alerts per hour, chosen by a rule fixed in the registration before it was applied -- the median by cost of the three grid points an axis that resolved can price -- and reported as one member of an admissible set rather than as an optimum
costaxis_hole_line: the highest coverage this instrument reaches, 0.6282 at theta 0.300, is priced by neither axis this campaign registered: the registered pass emitted no point at all, and the corpus-wide pass recorded at the deployed threshold cannot reach a grid point below it. Its only in-situ price comes from the 8-segment pass the allocation code selected without a registration, whose interval there spans [0.500, 28.812] alerts per hour -- a factor of 58 between its ends -- and returns exactly zero in 2.32 per cent of resamples
d5s_concl_line: Run for real on the verification sample, that point raised 1.7538 alerts per hour, outside the interval it was selected within, all of them on one of the eight segments
d5s_oos_line: Run for real at theta 0.525 on the eight segments of the verification sample, the fall channel raised 7 alerts in 3.9914 h, 1.7538 alerts per hour with a segment bootstrap of [0.000, 5.283], all of them on one substituted-clock segment, the same one that carried all 16 alerts this sample raised at the deployed threshold; on the corpus-wide pass that segment carries 16 of 91 alerts there and 6 of 44 at this point. The point estimate lies outside the interval [0.251, 0.844] the point was selected within, and is reported as a result rather than absorbed into the table. The sample is out-of-sample only against the sweep sample: all eight of its segments also lie inside the corpus-wide pass that priced the point
derived_line_native_clock: The complement, {\CntInsituSegmentsNativeClockDerived} segments on the container's own clock, is DERIVED by subtraction from the manifest and the registered substitution table, not counted directly: {\CntInsituSegmentsContainerFpsVerifiedInBand} segments record the container rate and are confirmed inside the band, while {\CntInsituSegmentsContainerFpsUnverifiable} measured before the HARNESS-5 fix record no container rate at all and cannot be checked individually. It is reported as a derived count and is never pooled with the {\CntInsituSegmentsOnSubstitutedClock} substituted segments.
deviation_line_clock: Container fps of {\CntInsituSegmentsOnSubstitutedClock}/{\CntInsituSegments} segments ({\CntInsituHoursOnSubstitutedClock}~h) lies outside [5,~60]; their observation time uses the decoded fps {\CntInsituSubstitutedFps} fixed before rescoring (HARNESS-5/9).
deviation_line_subst_pooled: {\CntFarSubstN} of {\CntInsituSegments} segments recorded 2026-08-31 08:00--13:00 carry a damaged H.264 bitstream and were rescored on a substituted clock, a frame rate registered before rescoring. The pre-registered test did not distinguish their alert rate from the native stratum's for any of the {\CntFarCheckersN} checkers, so they remain \emph{pooled} in the reported in-situ false-alarm rate over all {\CntFarPooledN} segments ({\CntFarPooledHours}~h); the per-stratum figures are given in the supplement.
deviation_line_subst_separated: {\CntFarSubstN} of {\CntInsituSegments} segments recorded 2026-08-31 08:00--13:00 carry a damaged H.264 bitstream: the container frame rate is unusable (HARNESS-5) and the decoder reports macroblock errors throughout. Their alert rate is separated from the in-situ false-alarm rate under pre-registration E4 as a \emph{recorder artefact}, the pre-registered comparison having placed the native point estimate outside the stratum's 95\% interval. The reported in-situ observation time is the {\CntFarNativeN} native segments ({\CntFarNativeHours}~h); the separated stratum is reported in full, with its own interval, in the supplement.

far_fall_a1_line: The A1 pass recorded FallChecker at its deployed decision point {\CntFarFallAOneRecordedTheta}, so the three grid points at or above it are exact over all {\CntInsituSegments} segments: {\CntFarFallAOneRateTZeroFourFive}, {\CntFarFallAOneRateTZeroFiveTwoFive} and {\CntFarFallAOneRateTZeroSixZero} alerts per hour. {\CntFarFallAOneAlertsBelowRecordedTheta} of {\CntFarFallAOneAlertsTotal} alerts carried a confidence at or below the recorded point, which is the count that decides whether the second disjunct of the decision rule ever fired on its own.

harness_sentence_clock: A guard that is correct at the layer it protects can still deadlock the whole system when no layer owns what it refuses: REFUSING is a perfect sentence to say to a person, and an unattended pass has no person in it.
harness_sentence_subst_pooled: The {\CntFarSubstN} segments whose container timing was unusable produced alerts at a rate the pre-registered test could not distinguish from the rest of the corpus, so the damage that corrupted their timing did not measurably reach the detector --- a negative result worth reporting, because the rule that would have removed them was written before it was known which way it would fall.
harness_sentence_subst_separated: A recorder that stores its camera's bitstream untouched preserves the damage along with the picture, and a detector cannot tell a reconstructed macroblock from a room: the defect that made {\CntFarSubstN} segments lie about their frame rate is the same defect that makes their alerts a measurement of the recorder.
